prompt:
Style: translucent-tracing-paper. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

- **artwork — simplification.** Only 2–5 essential visual memory cues are kept; about 75–90% of the secondary background is removed, and about 55–70% of the lower panel stays visually quiet, with a compact focal grouping and generous negative space. - **artwork — paper layering.** The subject is rendered in about 3–5 thin, semi-transparent, matte, softly milky tracing-paper layers with fine fibers, at three clarity levels: one gesture through a single layer; principal forms softened through two overlapping layers; secondary forms partly obscured under more layers. Softness comes from translucency and layered occlusion, not blur. - **artwork — color and light.** Colors are derived independently per photograph from its own palette over a clean off-white or very lightly source-tinted background, avoiding yellowing, sepia or aged-paper tones. Lighting follows the source, with broad soft light through the sheets and restrained translucent luminosity. - **What it avoids.** Realistic rendering, dense outlines, polygonal facets, watercolor blooms, heavy grain, glossy plastic, acrylic, frosted glass, thick cardboard, origami and paper-cut looks. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
reference_method: isolated single-source batch; image results withheld until all calls completed; per-image Git checkpoint
